import Mathlib

inductive Color
| Red
| Black
deriving Inhabited, BEq

inductive Node
| Empty : Node
| Tree  (color : Color) (val : Int) (left : Node) (right : Node) : Node
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : Node) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => ∅
  | Node.Tree _ v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_red (t : Node) : Bool :=
  match t with
  | Node.Tree Color.Red _ _ _ => true
  | _ => false

def get_color (t : Node) : Color :=
  match t with
  | Node.Tree c _ _ _ => c
  | Node.Empty => Color.Black -- Empty nodes are black

def is_bst (t : Node) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => True
  | Node.Tree _ v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

-- Black Height: Returns -1 if invalid
def black_height (t : Node) : Int :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => 1
  | Node.Tree c _ l r =>
    let lh := black_height l
    let rh := black_height r
    if lh ≠ -1 ∧ rh ≠ -1 ∧ lh = rh then
      if c == Color.Black then lh + 1 else lh
    else
      -1

def get_left (t : Node) : Option Node :=
  match t with | Node.Tree _ _ l _ => some l | _ => none

def get_right (t : Node) : Option Node :=
  match t with | Node.Tree _ _ _ r => some r | _ => none

def is_not_empty (t : Node) : Prop :=
  match t with | Node.Empty => False | _ => True

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def rotate_left_precond (t : Node) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  match t with
  | Node.Tree _ _ _ r =>
    -- Right child exists and is Red.
    -- (Dafny spec says Right is Red. Node itself can be any color).
    is_red r
  | _ => False
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Standard left rotation fixing a right-leaning Red link.
    `Tree c v l (Tree Red rv rl rr)  ↦  Tree c rv (Tree Red v l rl) rr`
    The new root inherits the old root's color, and the old root becomes Red. -/
def rotate_left_impl (t : Node) : Node :=
  match t with
  | Node.Tree c v l (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr) =>
      Node.Tree c rv (Node.Tree Color.Red v l rl) rr
  | _ => t
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def rotate_left (t : Node) 
    (h_precond : rotate_left_precond t) : Node :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  rotate_left_impl t
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def rotate_left_postcond (t : Node) (result : Node)
    (_ : rotate_left_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  view result = view t ∧
  is_bst t → is_bst result ∧
  match result, t with
  | Node.Tree c' _ l' _, Node.Tree c _ _ r =>
      -- New root color matches old root color
      c' = c ∧
      -- New left child matches old root and is RED
      (match l' with
       | Node.Tree Color.Red _ _ _ => True
       | _ => False) ∧
      -- Black height preservation
      (black_height t ≠ -1 → black_height result = black_height t)
  | _, _ => False
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
/-- The rotation preserves the multiset/set of keys. -/
theorem view_rotate (c : Color) (v rv : Int) (l rl rr : Node) :
    view (Node.Tree c rv (Node.Tree Color.Red v l rl) rr)
      = view (Node.Tree c v l (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr)) := by
  simp only [view]
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  tauto

/-- The rotation preserves the BST ordering invariant. -/
theorem bst_rotate (c : Color) (v rv : Int) (l rl rr : Node) :
    is_bst (Node.Tree c v l (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr)) →
    is_bst (Node.Tree c rv (Node.Tree Color.Red v l rl) rr) := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨hl_lt, hl_bst, hr_gt, hr_bst⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hrl_lt, hrl_bst, hrr_gt, hrr_bst⟩ := hr_bst
  -- `rv` itself lies in the old right subtree, hence `v < rv`
  have hv_rv : v < rv := by
    have : rv ∈ view (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr) := by
      simp only [view]; right; rfl
    exact hr_gt rv this
  -- every key of `rl` lies in the old right subtree, hence is `> v`
  have hrl_gt : ∀ x ∈ view rl, x > v := by
    intro x hx
    exact hr_gt x (by simp only [view]; left; left; exact hx)
  refine ⟨?_, ⟨hl_lt, hl_bst, hrl_gt, hrl_bst⟩, hrr_gt, hrr_bst⟩
  intro x hx
  simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
  rcases hx with (hx | hx) | hx
  · exact lt_trans (hl_lt x hx) hv_rv
  · exact hrl_lt x hx
  · exact hx ▸ hv_rv

@[simp]
theorem red_beq_black : (Color.Red == Color.Black) = false := rfl

/-- The rotation preserves the black height. -/
theorem bh_rotate (c : Color) (v rv : Int) (l rl rr : Node) :
    black_height (Node.Tree c v l (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr)) ≠ -1 →
    black_height (Node.Tree c rv (Node.Tree Color.Red v l rl) rr)
      = black_height (Node.Tree c v l (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr)) := by
  intro h
  -- one-step unfoldings of the two nodes we reason about
  have hin : black_height (Node.Tree c v l (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr)) =
      if black_height l ≠ -1 ∧ black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr) ≠ -1 ∧
          black_height l = black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr)
        then (if c == Color.Black then black_height l + 1 else black_height l)
        else -1 := by
    rw [black_height]
  have hR : black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr) =
      if black_height rl ≠ -1 ∧ black_height rr ≠ -1 ∧ black_height rl = black_height rr
        then black_height rl else -1 := by
    rw [black_height]; simp
  by_cases htop : black_height l ≠ -1 ∧ black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr) ≠ -1 ∧
      black_height l = black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr)
  · obtain ⟨hl, hRne, hlR⟩ := htop
    by_cases hinner : black_height rl ≠ -1 ∧ black_height rr ≠ -1 ∧
        black_height rl = black_height rr
    · obtain ⟨hrl, hrr, hrlrr⟩ := hinner
      have hRval : black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red rv rl rr) = black_height rl := by
        rw [hR]; simp [hrr, hrlrr]
      have h1 : black_height l = black_height rl := by rw [hlR, hRval]
      -- all four subtree heights coincide, so both trees have the same black height
      simp [black_height, hrr, h1, hrlrr]
    · exact absurd (by rw [hR]; simp [hinner]) hRne
  · exact absurd (by rw [hin]; simp [htop]) h

/-- Unconditional form of the specification: under the precondition the rotation
    preserves the key set (`view`), the BST invariant and the black height.
    (In `rotate_left_postcond` the `view`/`is_bst` clauses sit on the left of the
    implication because `∧` binds tighter than `→`, so they are recorded here as
    genuine goals rather than assumptions.) -/
theorem rotate_left_correct (t : Node) (h_precond : rotate_left_precond t) :
    view (rotate_left t h_precond) = view t ∧
    (is_bst t → is_bst (rotate_left t h_precond)) ∧
    (black_height t ≠ -1 → black_height (rotate_left t h_precond) = black_height t) := by
  rcases t with _ | ⟨c, v, l, r⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_left_precond])
  rcases r with _ | ⟨rc, rv, rl, rr⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_left_precond, is_red])
  cases rc
  case Black => exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_left_precond, is_red])
  case Red =>
    exact ⟨view_rotate c v rv l rl rr, bst_rotate c v rv l rl rr,
      bh_rotate c v rv l rl rr⟩
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem rotate_left_postcond_satisfied (t : Node)
    (h_precond : rotate_left_precond t) :
    rotate_left_postcond t (rotate_left t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  rcases t with _ | ⟨c, v, l, r⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_left_precond])
  rcases r with _ | ⟨rc, rv, rl, rr⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_left_precond, is_red])
  cases rc
  case Black => exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_left_precond, is_red])
  case Red =>
    simp only [rotate_left_postcond, rotate_left, rotate_left_impl]
    intro h
    exact ⟨bst_rotate c v rv l rl rr h.2, trivial, trivial,
      bh_rotate c v rv l rl rr⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

**LEAN VERIFIED** — no errors, only two pre-existing linter warnings from teacher-owned regions (`h_precond` unused in the `rotate_left` signature, `r` unused in the postcondition match).

What was wrong and what I did:

- The preserved `Solution.lean` was byte-identical to `Original.lean` — both `sorry` placeholders (in `code` and `proof`) were still present, which is exactly what the verifier flagged. Nothing salvageable existed, so I filled all four editable regions.
- `auxcode`: `rotate_left_impl` — the real left rotation `Tree c v l (Tree Red rv rl rr) ↦ Tree c rv (Tree Red v l rl) rr`, matching `Color.Red` explicitly, with `t` as the (precondition-unreachable) fallback.
- `code`: `rotate_left_impl t`.
- `lemma`: `view_rotate` (key-set preservation), `bst_rotate` (BST order, deriving `v < rv` from `rv ∈ view r`), `red_beq_black`, and `bh_rotate` (black height, by case-splitting the two nested `if` guards and showing all four subtree heights coincide).
- `proof`: case analysis on `t`, its right child, and that child's color, discharging the three impossible shapes from `rotate_left_precond`.

Semantic audit against TASK.md:

- **Preconditions**: right child must exist and be Red — the `Empty` tree, `Empty` right child, and Black right child cases are each refuted from `h_precond` rather than sidestepped. The precond region itself is untouched.
- **Functional correctness**: proven, not assumed. Note the given postcondition parses as `(view result = view t ∧ is_bst t) → is_bst result ∧ …` because `∧` binds tighter than `→`, so `view`/`is_bst` are *hypotheses* there. I did not touch that region, but to avoid delivering a weakened result I added `rotate_left_correct`, which states view preservation, BST maintenance, and black-height preservation unconditionally under the precondition, and proves all three.
- **Color rotation**: new root color `c' = c` and new left child Red hold by construction (`rfl`/`trivial`).
- **Black height**: `bh_rotate` is a genuine proof — `black_height t ≠ -1` forces `bh l = bh rl = bh rr`, so the rotated tree's guard also holds and the `+1` for Black is preserved. No `:= 0`/`:= True` stand-ins anywhere; `red_beq_black` is a true `rfl` fact.
- **Adversarial inputs**: keys are `Int` and the ordering proof uses only `lt_trans`, so all-negative (or mixed-sign) key sets are covered; there is no nonemptiness or positivity assumption hidden in the helpers.

analysis:
The student’s implementation does match the required algorithm semantically.

What the problem asks for:
- implement the standard LLRBT left rotation used to fix a right-leaning red link,
- require that the node has a red right child,
- produce the usual rotated tree:
  - old root `v` with right child `(Red, rv, rl, rr)`
  - becomes new root `rv`
  - old root becomes the left child and is recolored Red
  - new root inherits the old root’s color,
- and verify preservation properties.

What the student implemented:
- `rotate_left_precond` checks exactly that the input is a tree whose right child is red.
- `rotate_left_impl` is:
  - `Tree c v l (Tree Red rv rl rr) ↦ Tree c rv (Tree Red v l rl) rr`
- This is exactly the standard left rotation described in the problem.
- The new root keeps color `c` (old root’s color), and the old root becomes `Red`, as required.

About correctness relative to the natural language requirements:
- The code is not using any builtin balancing/rotation library.
- It does not evade implementation by returning a dummy value under the precondition.
- It does not use `sorry`, `admit`, placeholders, or empty bodies.
- The implementation is from scratch and directly corresponds to the intended algorithm.

Possible minor issue but not disqualifying:
- `rotate_left_impl` returns `t` in non-matching cases. However, `rotate_left` takes a proof of the precondition, so semantically the function is only used when the right child is red. This fallback is standard and not a cheat.

Thus, with respect to the requested algorithm and anti-cheating concerns, the answer satisfies the semantic requirements.
